text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PROD ALERT: gpu-pool-west autoscaler hit MAX_NODES=45, pending pods > 1800 for 12m, surge throttling detected. Dashboard: https://grafana/redwood/d/gpu-pool-west. Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/incidents/autoscale

jules_oncall: I'm taking this. Noted.

sam_sre: Joining. Quick check: is this caused by scheduled batch or sudden API spike?

jules_oncall: Graphs show both. There was a scheduled analytics job + unexpected traffic spike from onboarding flow. Autoscaler logs show repeated "scale limit reached" messages.

leo_infra: Confirmed. Cloud provider returned quota/zone allocation warnings and we hit nodePool.maxNodes=45. Provider also returning transient 'Insufficient resources' for GPU machine types in the zone.

maya_prodeng: Support flagged a few customers reporting 5xxs. Need customer comms if this impacts SLAs.

jules_oncall: Copy. I'm running diagnostics.

```# hpa status
$ kubectl get hpa -n inference gpu-pool-hpa -o jsonpath='{.status}'
currentReplicas: 45
desiredReplicas: 45
conditions: ScalingLimited: reason=MaxNodesReached
```

$ kubectl get pods -n inference --field-selector=status.phase=Pending | head -n 5
pod/worker-abc Pending  ContainerCreating   0/1  -  22m
pod/worker-def Pending  ContainerCreating   0/1  -  19m
... (1800+ pending)

sam_sre: Two immediate mitigations: 1) try manual node pool max increase (runtime ~10-15m) 2) apply routing throttles + fallback to cpu-only model for background batch jobs to relieve GPU pressure. Which do we want first?

jules_oncall: Let's do both in parallel. Leo, can infra approve a manual increase for Hosted? Policy needs infra lead + oncall.

leo_infra: I approve technically but note provider is rate-limited. If we request a jump to 75 nodes we might still get slow provisioning. I'll approve raising to 70 to give some buffer.

maya_prodeng: Approve from product. I'll prepare a short customer note: "We're increasing capacity to address degraded inference performance; you may see retries while we recover."

ci-bot: Noted. Initiating terraform change request from jules_oncall.

jules_oncall: Terraform snippet:

```
resource "azurerm_kubernetes_cluster_node_pool" "gpu_pool" {
  name = "gpu-pool"
  min_count = 4
  max_count = 70
}
```

Applying terraform now. ETA nodes ~12m (provider backoff may add time).

sam_sre: While nodes are provisioning, executing routing policy changes to protect API: lower batch priority, set fallback route for non-critical endpoints. Patch: 

```
PATCH /routing/policies/gpu-pool
{"priority_override": "low", "fallback_model": "cpu-approx-v2", "throttle": "60%"}
```

sam_sre: Also adding temporary circuit breaker on large-infer endpoints.

(6 minutes in)

leo_infra: Provider status: attempting allocation. Getting a mix of preemptible and spot capacity. Some zones are depleted; spinning up nodes across adjacent zones.

jules_oncall: Observing pending pods drop: 1800 -> 560. Latency still elevated but improving. 5xxs trending down.

maya_prodeng: Support: customer C reports some requests retried but now success rate improving.

(12 minutes in)

ci-bot: Terraform apply completed. Node pool max_count set to 70. Initiated scale-up.

leo_infra: New nodes are starting. Note: some nodes are spot; we'll monitor preemption risk. Provisioning time ~11m.

```
$ kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-pool --no-headers | wc -l
68
```

sam_sre: Pending pods now 34. Queue drain visible. 429 spikes stopped.

jules_oncall: Great. Let's keep fallback routing for 30m then roll back if stable.

maya_prodeng: Drafting customer update: "We've increased GPU capacity and applied temporary routing to prioritize API traffic. We're monitoring and will follow up with a timeline."

leo_infra: Action items: - Postmortem to cover: provider zone depletion + scheduled job hitting prod pool during peak - Add quota/zone awareness to autoscaler - Consider emergency burst pool in different zone/instance family - Make manual cap-raise runbook shorter and pre-approved for oncall with infra guardrails.

sam_sre: Also propose runtime change: allow autoscaler to request cross-zone allocation more aggressively if single-zone capacity is exhausted.

jules_oncall: Incident logged IR-2026-03-15-gpu-burst. Tagging: autoscale, gpu, manual-override, customer-impact. Postmortem owner: sam_sre. Draft due in 72h.

maya_prodeng: Customer comms sent. Will follow-up with affected customers with root cause and remediation timeline.

leo_infra: I'll file infra ticket to provision a small warm standby burst-pool of durable nodes (not spot) to shave recovery time.

jules_oncall: Handing over for follow-up. If anything regresses ping me. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

sam_sre: Closing active mitigation. Monitor for 2 hours before de-escalation.

(Incident wrapped)
